title: Farewell to Sam Faddis — Patriot, Truth Teller, and Friend
summary:
Farewell to Sam Faddis — Patriot, Truth Teller, and Friend

America has lost a friend and a patriot, and so have I. Sam Faddis—retired CIA operations officer, frequent guest on this show, and a man who became my friend even though I never met him in person—passed away quietly at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia on the evening of July 25, 2026 with his wife, four children, and family by his side. I read the statement from his family, who asked for privacy and thanked the doctors, medical staff, and all of you for your prayers and support. I first came across Sam through Hillsdale College’s free Imprimis, where he wrote about what had gone wrong at the CIA and how to fix it—brave, objective, and always productive. Sam told the truth about everything, including how to right this ship. We’ll miss him terribly.

summary:
NJ MVC Software Error Registered 6,600 Noncitizens to Vote—Why No Prosecutions?

Mark Garrett of Your LEO Nation reacts to a New Jersey press conference with Lieutenant Governor Caldwell and MVC acting chair Rosalie Johnson, where the governor disclosed a serious MVC software error that allegedly improperly registered about 6,600 noncitizens to vote between June 2023 and June 2024, with an initial analysis indicating fewer than 400 of those individuals voted. Garrett says the governor is using “accountability” language while blaming predecessors and Donald Trump, but failed to include any prosecutors on stage and showed no intent to prosecute those who voted illegally—an indictable third-degree offense carrying 3–5 years and up to $15,000 in penalties. He also claims the governor will not share identifying information with the federal government for removal and urges viewers to comment.

title: California’s Exodus & the Collapse of the Rule of Law
summary:
California’s Exodus & the Collapse of the Rule of Law | Your LEO Nation w/ Mark Garrett

Mark Garrett of Your LEO Nation discusses California’s net population loss since 2020 and argues the outflow is driven by high housing and gas costs, crime, and policies he says attract non-citizens through welfare and sanctuary laws. He describes who is leaving—middle and lower income earners, retirees, conservatives, and major companies relocating headquarters to states like Texas and Tennessee. Garrett focuses on law enforcement, citing a steep drop in sworn officers, especially at LAPD, and links low morale and departures to understaffing, burnout, leadership issues, and criminal justice changes such as Prop 47, Prop 57, and AB 392. He warns of a downward cycle of fewer officers, slower responses, more crime, and shrinking tax bases, and asks current and former California officers to share their experiences after moving to states like Texas, Florida, Tennessee, and Arizona.

title: The 2011 Realignment of Adult Felony Populations: Results and Key Takeaways
summary: In 2011, California shifted responsibility for incarcerating and supervising certain adult felony populations from the state to counties. The state also shifted a portion of tax revenues to counties to cover the additional costs. These changes were part of a larger shift of responsibilities known as the 2011 realignment. Pursuant to Chapter 96 of 2023 (AB 1080, Ta), this report provides information on how various aspects of the realignment of adult felony populations have been implemented and evaluates the results.

title: Annual Report on Tax Exemptions for Medicinal Cannabis
summary: Chapter 920 of 2024 (AB 2555, Quirk-Silva) renewed an existing tax exemption for certain donations of medical cannabis products. The law directs our office to submit an annual report containing data on three outcomes related to the exemptions: the number of medicinal cannabis patients served, the amount of medicinal cannabis products donated, and the amount of tax revenue lost. This report fulfills that statutory requirement for 2025.
